references.name: Jim Rogers
references.desc:
Hot Commodities (2004);
      Rogers International Commodities Index
references.connection:
Created RICI (36 commodities; 473% returns 1998–2022);
      the original case for the 21st-century commodity bull market

references.name: Lakshmi Mittal
references.connection:
Engineered the hostile takeover of Arcelor to create the
      world's largest steel company — the defining mining M&A
      event of the 2000s

references.name: Alan Greenspan
references.connection:
Coined "irrational exuberance" to describe speculative excess;
      cited in the context of speculative risk in commodity futures markets

references.name: Elon Musk
references.connection:
Led the EV revolution starting 2008; changed the demand
      outlook for copper, lithium, and palladium

references.name: Francisco Pizarro
references.connection:
Gold-motivated conquest of the Inca civilization (1524) —
      the historical anchor for the argument that commodities have
      shaped human civilization more than any other force

references.name: Winston Churchill
references.connection:
Ordered conversion of the British Navy from coal to oil,
      heralding the modern Hydrocarbon Age and permanently shifting
      global commodity balances

references.name: BP / British Petroleum
references.connection:
Rebranded as "Beyond Petroleum" — cited as an example of
      the energy transition reshaping the self-presentation of the
      world's largest commodity companies

references.name: Energy Information Administration
references.desc: Statistical branch of the US Department of Energy
references.connection:
Publishes the Wednesday oil inventory reports — the most
      market-moving weekly data release in energy markets

references.name: Commodity Futures Trading Commission
references.connection:
Regulates futures markets; publishes the Commitment of
      Traders report that reveals speculative vs. commercial
      positioning

references.name: Refco
references.connection:
Cited as a corporate governance risk example — hid debts
      and losses in offshore accounts before collapse, emphasizing
      the need to research any firm before investing

references.name: Rothschild banking family
references.connection:
Financed the original mining operations that became one of
      the world's largest diversified mining companies — illustrating
      commodity capital's deep historical roots

references.name: PIMCO
references.connection:
Manages the PIMCO Commodity Real Return Strategy Fund
      (PCRAX) — the largest commodity-oriented mutual fund at
      $30+ billion AUM
